clue.text: Bite hard in competition

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for hard is placed inside the word for competition

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A contestant bites down hard during a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To chomp is to bite down noisily, a synonym for biting.

clue.text: Something fattening from the East on a spring vegetable

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another follows it, so the turned piece comes after

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: read from the east in an across entry means read right to left, backwards

parts.note: sugar is a fattening food

explanation.surface: Someone tops a spring vegetable with something rich imported from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something fattening' tempts you toward a rich food in the surface; 'from the East' reverses it, and 'on' in an across entry places that piece after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is an example of a vegetable, eaten as spears in spring.

clue.text: Tory hunt lobby

parts.note: con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
to course is to hunt game with dogs

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician lobbies against a ban on hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a large open hall or foyer, much like a lobby.

clue.text: Copper street fighting, not entirely an uncommon thing

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a riot is fighting in the streets

explanation.surface: A policeman caught up in street fighting is a rare sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: A curio is a rare or unusual object, a curiosity.

clue.text: Old writer the Queen is the first to receive?

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: An elderly author is the first to be given something by Her Majesty.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the opening batter is first to receive the bowling, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening batsman is the player who first faces the bowling in cricket.

clue.text: Antelope seconds away from Wuthering Heights?

indicators.note: the second letters of each word are removed, R from the author's name and O from the book

parts.note: Wuthering Heights is a Bronte book, by Emily Bronte

explanation.surface: A gazelle-like animal wanders off the Yorkshire moors.
explanation.walkthrough: BRONTE BOOK loses the second letter of each word (R and O).
explanation.definitionFit: The bontebok is a South African species of antelope.

clue.text: Not leaving the house, as engineers are not to be trusted

parts.note: someone not going out is in
as and since both mean because
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Engineers who stay indoors are shifty characters.
explanation.definitionFit: Insincere describes someone false or hypocritical, so untrustworthy.

clue.text: Monarch is to regret accepting Liberal Republican

indicators.note: accepting means the word for regret takes in the letter for Liberal

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A king regrets taking on politicians from rival parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler is a sovereign or monarch who governs a country.

clue.text: Brown bread for good health, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a drink raised to someone's good health

explanation.definitionFit: Toast is both grilled bread and a drink proposed in someone's honour.

clue.text: Swats creepy-crawly for simple entertainment

parts.note: to swat is to slap
a tick is a small bug

explanation.surface: Someone flailing at insects provides crude amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick is broad physical comedy, a simple form of entertainment.

clue.text: What helps a chap focus, say, embracing the old girl

indicators.note: embracing means the abbreviation for say wraps round the old word for the

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
ye is an archaic form of the
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A man squints to bring an old girlfriend into view.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeglass, or monocle, is a lens that helps a wearer see clearly.

clue.text: Footballer's good for the time of season

indicators.note: good for time means the letter for good replaces the letter for time

parts.note: winter is a season of the year

explanation.surface: A football player is fit for the season ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A winger plays on the wing in football.

clue.text: Start to examine scrawny tree

indicators.note: start to means just the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: scrawny and bony both mean thin

explanation.surface: Inspecting a thin, sickly tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a tropical tree yielding dark hardwood.

clue.text: Supply nothing that is without singular balance

parts.note: to equip is to supply
O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the abbreviation for that is goes round the letter

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Providing nothing leaves things unbalanced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is in its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipoise is a state of equal balance or equilibrium.

clue.text: Central parts of Institute reforms dictating payment in kind

indicators.note: central parts means the middle three letters of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Reforms at an institute insist on bartering.
explanation.definitionFit: Tit for tat means retaliation in kind, repaying like with like.

clue.text: Moral panic's not fine

indicators.note: not fine means the letter for fine is dropped from the word

parts.note: fright is panic; the 's stands for is
F is short for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A moral panic is said to be unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Right as an adjective means morally good or just.

clue.text: Mad at home to see uninvited intruder

parts.note: cuckoo is slang for mad
a bird at home is in its nest

explanation.surface: Someone at home is furious to find a gatecrasher.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuckoo in the nest is an unwelcome presence displacing the rightful occupants.

clue.text: So unceremoniously exhibiting large cat

indicators.note: exhibiting means the letters are on show inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A big cat is shown off without ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a large cat.

clue.text: What's needed to build muscle Dicky tore in leg

indicators.note: in places the jumbled word inside the word for leg

parts.note: pin is slang for leg

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for weak or faulty, signalling a muddled order

explanation.surface: A bodybuilder with a dodgy leg tore a muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' makes ROTE from TORE, put 'in' PIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Protein is the nutrient the body uses to build muscle tissue.

clue.text: Character regularly encountered in taqueria

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A personality met often at a Mexican taco bar.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is a distinctive atmosphere or character around something.

clue.text: Most unusual finding man with Latin name in China

indicators.note: in puts the pieces inside the slang word for friend

parts.note: china, from rhyming slang china plate = mate, means pal
he refers to a man
nomen is Latin for name

explanation.surface: A remarkable discovery of a man with a Latin name in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; it is rhyming slang, china plate for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomenal means extraordinary, exceptional in the highest degree.

clue.text: One storytelling author, not the first to hold church up

indicators.note: to hold means the shortened word contains the turned piece
not the first drops the opening letter of the word

parts.note: a writer is an author

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A novelist, not the top one, supports a church.
explanation.walkthrough: WRITER loses its first letter ('not the first'), and the church turned 'up' gives EC.
explanation.definitionFit: A reciter is someone who narrates or recites stories aloud.

clue.text: Soldier shuts up a rude patriot

indicators.note: shuts up means the soldier's letters enclose the rest

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
ribald means coarse or rude

explanation.surface: A soldier silences a vulgar nationalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Garibaldi was the Italian patriot who led the unification of Italy.

clue.text: Cattle stopped running on river area where the rich live

parts.note: stock means farm animals, cattle
a machine that broke stopped working
a belt is a zone or area

explanation.surface: Cattle stopped running beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: A STOCKBROKER BELT is a wealthy commuter area outside London; 'on' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: The stockbroker belt is the prosperous commuter suburbs where affluent people live.

clue.text: Determined half of champers is Spanish wine

indicators.note: half of means the second four letters of champers

parts.note: tent is a red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: Someone resolved that a half bottle of fizz is Spanish.
explanation.walkthrough: Champers is British slang for champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistent means continuing firmly, determined.

clue.text: Pot caused drunk to be disorientated

indicators.note: drunk suggests letters staggering into a new order

explanation.surface: Cannabis made someone confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaced out is slang for dazed and disorientated.

clue.text: Quite gutless youth stopping to cry at blood sports

indicators.note: stopping means the pieces plug the gap within the word to

parts.note: all and quite both mean completely

indicators.note: gutless means the inner letters are removed, leaving the outer two

explanation.surface: A rather cowardly lad stops crying out at a hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Tally-ho is the huntsman's cry on sighting a fox.

clue.text: Small fish head for trawler?

parts.note: a kipper is a smoked herring

explanation.surface: A small fish heads for a fishing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is the captain or head of a boat, such as a trawler.

clue.text: Thames location hasn't the right conditions for racing

indicators.note: hasn't the means the letter for right is missing from the town name

parts.note: Goring is a village on the River Thames

explanation.surface: A riverside town lacks the right conditions for a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The going is the state of the ground in horse racing.

clue.text: Give up, utterly lacking in energy

indicators.note: lacking in means the energy letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: quite means utterly or completely
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone gives up, totally drained of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit means to give up or abandon something.
